slides.1.title: Portugal's 14 Official Wine Regions
slides.1.html:
According to the IVV (Portuguese Wine Institute), Portugal has 14 wine regions, each of which may contain several DOCs (legally defined appellations).

🗺️ North (Norte)

  • Minho: home of Vinho Verde, Portugal's largest DOC, with 9 sub-regions
  • Trás-os-Montes: remote mountains in the northeast, continental climate
  • Douro / Porto: UNESCO-listed terraces and the original home of Port, demarcated in 1756 (the earliest region under continuous regulation)

⛰️ North-Central (Centro Norte)

  • Terras de Cister: includes Távora-Varosa (Portugal's highest-altitude region)
  • Beira Atlântico: includes Bairrada and Dão
  • Terras do Dão: granite highlands, the heart of Dão DOC
  • Terras da Beira: includes Beira Interior, with rugged mountain terrain

🌊 Central West Coast

  • Lisboa: 9 sub-regions around Lisbon with diverse soils
  • Tejo: the Tagus Valley, formerly known as Ribatejo
  • Península de Setúbal: famous for Moscatel de Setúbal sweet wine

☀️ South (Sul)

  • Alentejo: vast plains, 8 sub-regions, the fastest-growing in recent times
  • Algarve: the far south, 4 DOCs, holiday-resort wines

🏝️ Islands (Ilhas)

  • Madeira: an Atlantic volcanic island, world-famous for oxidative fortified wine
  • Açores: the Azores archipelago, volcanic basalt, with the Pico Island DOC

slides.4.title: North vs. South: Climate and Style Contrasts
slides.4.items.0.label: North (Minho / Douro)
slides.4.items.0.desc: Humid Atlantic, rainfall up to 1,500mm, crisp high-acid whites
slides.4.items.1.label: Centre (Dão / Bairrada)
slides.4.items.1.desc: Sheltered by mountains, continental, granite soils, structured reds
slides.4.items.2.label: South (Alentejo / Algarve)
slides.4.items.2.desc: Mediterranean, hot and dry, rainfall under 500mm, rich and round reds
slides.4.items.3.label: Islands (Madeira / Açores)
slides.4.items.3.desc: Maritime Atlantic, volcanic soils, fortified wines and distinctive whites

slides.6.question: Which of the following is Portugal's largest DOC (by area)?
slides.6.explanation: Vinho Verde lies in the Minho region of northwest Portugal and is the country's largest DOC, covering about 21,000 hectares.
slides.7.question: In the "portugal-regions-overview" exploration, which Portuguese region lies on an Atlantic volcanic island and is world-famous for fortified wine?
slides.7.explanation: Madeira lies on a volcanic island in the Atlantic, 1,000 km west of Portugal, and is famous worldwide for the fortified wine of the same name. The unique estufagem heating process gives Madeira caramel, nut and citrus-peel aromas and an extraordinary ageing potential of 100+ years. The other island region, Açores, also lies in the Atlantic.
